title: Book Three · Chapter 65: A Little of His Own
story:
Two weeks later, the afternoons grow cooler.

Ronan has made two more short trips for Mum. One bag went to Mrs Deng. The other went to a customer near the tea shop.

On Saturday, Mum puts a few coins beside his breakfast bowl.

“For the trips.”

Ronan looks at them. “I can help.”

“You did. I finished another piece of work while you went.”

She takes a small envelope from her box.

“We can do this for one or two short trips on Saturday. Not every afternoon.”

Ronan moves the coins into the envelope. He thinks of a bus seat beside Leo and a new city outside the window.

“I could save for a visit.”

Mum nods. “A start.”

“Not enough yet.”

“No.”

She puts the rest of her money near her work sheet. Part goes into another envelope. She leaves some beside the cloth and thread.

Ronan watches her count.

“The coats brought all that?”

“Several coats. And some of it goes back into the work.”

She shows him a piece of lining and a packet of needles. Then she puts the household money away.

Dad comes in from the yard. He is ready to leave for Mr Sun's place.

“A rich breakfast?” he asks.

“Only my side of the table,” Ronan says.

Dad looks at the little envelope.

“Then you can buy the whole street.”

“The street may have to be small.”

Mum laughs. Dad takes his work bag and leaves.

Ronan counts his own coins once. He wants a cold drink later, but he puts most of them back. He keeps only a little spending money in his pocket.

That morning, he finishes his answer to Leo. He writes about the fruit shop, the oranges, and Mum's busy Saturdays.

He also asks about the other city's winter. He has only seen it through Leo's words and the two roof drawings.

Ronan sends the eleventh letter before lunch. At the shop corner, he looks at the small treats beside the window.

He buys one piece of sweet bread with his pocket money. The envelope stays at home.

When he returns, Mum is fitting Mrs Deng's trousers. The woman stands on a low step while Mum checks the length.

Ronan waits outside with his bread. He can hear the women discuss the shoes that will go with the trousers.

After the customer leaves, Mum puts the garment beside her work sheet.

“Another Saturday?” Ronan asks.

“I will tell you when it is ready.”

He nods and takes his own book to the sunny part of the yard. The bread is nearly gone, but the coins in his envelope are still there.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

save＝存下、攒钱；household＝家庭的、家用的；spending money＝零花钱；garment＝一件衣服。

## 理解问题

1. Mum为什么给Ronan一点报酬？他们说好的帮助范围有多大？
2. Ronan有没有把所有收入都花掉？家里收到的衣服款项又是不是全都能随意花？

## 读句子

**He keeps only a little spending money in his pocket.**

拆开看：He / keeps only a little spending money / in his pocket.

他／只留下少量零花钱／放在口袋里。
